## Measurement spec

`spec:A3`

| field | value |
|---|---|

| collector_pin | scrapy>=2.11 |

| instrument_state | specified |
| leg | A3 |
| mode | auto |
| prior_art | `w3c-dwbp-2017` |
| rf_ask_plain | Links on the data page to one zipped or complete file holding the whole dataset. |
| rf_fail | Every linked file on the same website, in the page's HTML as first served (a download behind a script-driven button or a form is not seen), was checked, and none is an archive or a non-web-page file without a query of at least fifty kibibytes. The two tests are stand-ins: a link with a query may still deliver the whole product, and a complete product smaller than fifty kibibytes fails the size floor. It is not a claim that the agency's downloads are partial, nor that no bulk download exists elsewhere, such as a data portal, an FTP site, or a bulk endpoint on a data interface. |
| rf_fix_line | Link a bulk download of the product from the product page. |
| rf_hypothesis | Can the whole dataset be retrieved in one request? An SI client that must assemble a product from many filtered queries makes many calls, can miss parts, and cannot tell when it has all of it; a bulk file answers that in one request. |
| rf_name_brief | The whole dataset in one download |
| rf_not_measured | The public client could not look at one or more of the linked files, for one of three reasons: the host refused the identified client; the client's own compliance with the site's robots.txt kept it from the file; or it could not confirm the absence because the page carried more same-website links than the cap of twenty-five, or a server or network error occurred. |
| rf_partial | Some of the agency's data pages linked such a whole-product download and some did not. |
| rf_pass | This data page links, on its own website, an archive file (named by its extension) or a file that is not a web page, carries no query in its address, and is at least fifty kibibytes. It is not verified to be the complete product. Every data page that was looked at met this. |
| rf_plain_name | Page links an archive or large unfiltered file |
| rf_question | Can the whole dataset be retrieved in a single request, rather than assembled piece by piece from many filtered queries? |
| rf_requirements | [{"source": "w3c-dwbp-2017", "quote": "Enable consumers to retrieve the full dataset with a single request."}, {"source": "omb-m-23-22-digital-first-public-experience", "quote": "making that information available as machine-readable data that can be accessed in bulk"}, {"source": "omb-m-23-22-digital-first-public-experience", "quote": "If an agency detects significant public interest in scraping information from web pages, the agency should strongly consider making that information available as machine-readable data that can be accessed in bulk"}] |
| rf_rung_two_changes | Nothing: this check needs no key. |
| rf_state | specified |
| rf_tells_plain | Whether someone can take all of it at once instead of piecing it together query by query. |
| rf_what_client_does | The public client opens the data page and then, for each file linked on it that lives on the same website (up to twenty-five), makes one quick web request asking about that file's type, its size, and whether its address carries a query, at one request per second. |
| rf_where_we_look | On the agency's data page, and the files linked from that page that sit on the same website as the page itself. |
| rf_who_else | Google Lighthouse runs this kind of check: anyone can run its automated checks against a named page, its criteria are published, and a result comes back met, not met, or not applicable. It does not run this exact one. |
| rf_why_it_matters | A Data on the Web Best Practice says to let consumers retrieve the full dataset with a single request, and an OMB memo says that where there is significant public interest in taking information off an agency's pages, the agency should strongly consider offering it in bulk; the fifty kibibytes floor and the query-means-filtered rule are the project's own choices. |
| rf_why_short | The World Wide Web Consortium's data guidance asks that a full dataset come in one request, and an OMB memo urges offering whole datasets for download. |
| rule_id | RULE-A3-v8 |
| signal | Crawl the product page one hop; classify links as bulk (whole-product archive or full dataset file) vs filtered query. |
